symptoms.name: Abdominal pain
symptoms.likely_causes: Gastritis, IBS, appendicitis, kidney stones, pancreatitis, hernia
symptoms.red_flags: Severe sharp pain, fever, vomiting blood, rigid abdomen
symptoms.self_care: Rest, heat pad, bland diet, hydration, avoid NSAIDs initially
symptoms.male_notes: Consider appendicitis, kidney stones, IBS equally
symptoms.female_notes: Consider menstrual cramping, ovulation pain, endometriosis, pelvic inflammatory disease
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Severe pain, lasts >24 hours, accompanied by fever/vomiting

symptoms.name: Anxiety
symptoms.likely_causes: Stress, life changes, underlying anxiety disorder
symptoms.red_flags: Panic with chest pain/breathlessness, or thoughts of self-harm
symptoms.self_care: Breathing exercises, reduce stimulants, talk to someone trusted
symptoms.male_notes: Often presents as irritability/anger. Underdiagnosed. May manifest as physical symptoms
symptoms.female_notes: More likely diagnosed. Linked to hormonal cycles. Postpartum anxiety/depression common
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Interferes with daily life or persists

symptoms.name: Back pain
symptoms.likely_causes: Muscle strain, herniated disc, poor posture, osteoarthritis, kidney stones
symptoms.red_flags: Severe pain, leg numbness/weakness, loss of bowel control
symptoms.self_care: Rest, heat/ice therapy, proper posture, stretching, core strengthening
symptoms.male_notes: Often work-related muscle strain. Disc herniation more common
symptoms.female_notes: Pregnancy-related sacroiliac pain common. Osteoporosis risk postmenopause
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Severe pain, accompanied by numbness/weakness, or follows trauma

symptoms.name: Bloating/gas
symptoms.likely_causes: Diet, food intolerance, swallowing air, digestive disorders
symptoms.red_flags: Bloating with severe pain or vomiting
symptoms.self_care: Smaller meals, limit gas-producing foods, gentle walking
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persistent or worsening despite diet changes

symptoms.name: Blood in stool
symptoms.likely_causes: Hemorrhoids, GI infection, ulcers, more serious GI conditions
symptoms.red_flags: Large amounts of blood, black tarry stool, dizziness/fainting
symptoms.self_care: Note color/amount, avoid straining
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Any occurrence should be medically evaluated

symptoms.name: Blood in urine
symptoms.likely_causes: UTI, kidney stones, strenuous exercise, more serious causes
symptoms.red_flags: Blood in urine with severe pain or inability to urinate
symptoms.self_care: Note frequency/amount, stay hydrated
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Any occurrence should be medically evaluated

symptoms.name: Blurred vision
symptoms.likely_causes: Eye strain, dry eyes, refractive error, migraine
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden vision loss/change, especially one-sided
symptoms.self_care: Rest eyes, reduce screen time, adequate lighting
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Sudden onset or persistent change

symptoms.name: Chest pain
symptoms.likely_causes: Muscle strain, acid reflux, anxiety, heart-related causes
symptoms.red_flags: Pressure/tightness radiating to arm/jaw, sweating, breathlessness
symptoms.self_care: Rest and stop exertion; do not self-diagnose
symptoms.male_notes: Classic crushing/pressure pain more likely. Higher cardiac risk age 45+
symptoms.female_notes: Often atypical: sharp, indigestion-like, fatigue, shortness of breath. Higher risk postmenopause
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Any unexplained chest pain warrants prompt evaluation

symptoms.name: Chills
symptoms.likely_causes: Fever onset, cold exposure, infection
symptoms.red_flags: Chills with high fever and confusion
symptoms.self_care: Warm layers, warm fluids, rest
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Recurrent chills with fever over 48 hours

symptoms.name: Congestion
symptoms.likely_causes: Common cold, flu, allergies, sinusitis, nasal polyps
symptoms.red_flags: High fever, severe headache, facial swelling
symptoms.self_care: Saline nasal drops, humidifier, steam inhalation, hydration
symptoms.male_notes: Usually viral/allergic. Sinusitis more common in women
symptoms.female_notes: Hormonal nasal congestion during menstrual cycle. Pregnancy rhinitis common
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts >2 weeks, accompanied by high fever or facial pain

symptoms.name: Constipation
symptoms.likely_causes: Low fiber diet, dehydration, inactivity, medication
symptoms.red_flags: Severe pain, inability to pass gas/stool, vomiting
symptoms.self_care: Increase fiber and water intake, gentle activity
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts more than a week or with severe pain

symptoms.name: Cough
symptoms.likely_causes: Common cold, flu, pneumonia, asthma, GERD, smoking, allergies
symptoms.red_flags: Bloody phlegm, severe shortness of breath, chest pain
symptoms.self_care: Hydration, honey, throat lozenges, humidifier, steam inhalation
symptoms.male_notes: Smokers at higher risk. Occupational exposure consideration
symptoms.female_notes: ACE inhibitor side effect more common in women. Pregnancy affects cough reflex
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts >3 weeks, productive with discolored sputum, or with fever >101°F

symptoms.name: Cough (dry)
symptoms.likely_causes: Viral infection, allergies, irritants, acid reflux
symptoms.red_flags: Cough with blood, severe breathlessness, or chest pain
symptoms.self_care: Honey/warm fluids, humidifier, avoid irritants
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts more than 3 weeks

symptoms.name: Cough (productive/phlegm)
symptoms.likely_causes: Bacterial/viral chest infection, bronchitis
symptoms.red_flags: Green/bloody phlegm with high fever and breathlessness
symptoms.self_care: Fluids, rest, steam inhalation
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Phlegm is discolored/bloody or persists beyond 10 days

symptoms.name: Depression/low mood
symptoms.likely_causes: Stress, life events, underlying mood disorder
symptoms.red_flags: Thoughts of self-harm or hopelessness
symptoms.self_care: Stay connected with others, gentle routine, sunlight/activity
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persists beyond 2 weeks or affects daily functioning

symptoms.name: Diarrhea
symptoms.likely_causes: Infection, food intolerance, medication side effect, stress
symptoms.red_flags: Blood in stool, high fever, signs of severe dehydration
symptoms.self_care: Oral rehydration fluids, bland diet (BRAT), rest
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts more than 2 days or with blood/fever

symptoms.name: Dizziness
symptoms.likely_causes: Dehydration, low blood pressure, inner ear issues, low blood sugar
symptoms.red_flags: Dizziness with chest pain, slurred speech, or one-sided weakness
symptoms.self_care: Sit/lie down, hydrate, avoid sudden movements
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Recurrent episodes or accompanied by fainting

symptoms.name: Dry skin
symptoms.likely_causes: Weather, dehydration, harsh soap, skin conditions
symptoms.red_flags: Cracking with signs of infection (redness, pus)
symptoms.self_care: Moisturize regularly, lukewarm showers, hydrate
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persistent cracking or signs of infection

symptoms.name: Ear pain
symptoms.likely_causes: Ear infection, fluid buildup, wax blockage, air pressure changes
symptoms.red_flags: Severe pain with high fever, swelling behind ear, or fluid discharge
symptoms.self_care: Warm compress, avoid inserting objects in ear
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Pain persists over 2 days or with fever/discharge

symptoms.name: Excessive bruising
symptoms.likely_causes: Minor trauma, blood thinners, vitamin deficiency, clotting issues
symptoms.red_flags: Bruising with no clear cause, or with unusual bleeding elsewhere
symptoms.self_care: Ice pack initially, elevate area, monitor
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Frequent unexplained bruising

symptoms.name: Eye redness/irritation
symptoms.likely_causes: Allergies, dryness, infection (conjunctivitis), irritant exposure
symptoms.red_flags: Severe pain, vision changes, or thick discharge
symptoms.self_care: Cool compress, avoid rubbing, artificial tears
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persists beyond a few days or with pain/vision changes

symptoms.name: Fatigue
symptoms.likely_causes: Poor sleep, anemia, stress, thyroid issues, viral illness, overtraining
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden extreme fatigue with chest pain or fainting
symptoms.self_care: Prioritize sleep, hydrate, balanced meals, moderate activity
symptoms.male_notes: Often indicates infection or serious condition. May mask depression initially
symptoms.female_notes: Common with anemia, thyroid issues, hormonal imbalances, menstrual cycle. Iron deficiency more common
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persists beyond 2 weeks or interferes with daily life

symptoms.name: Fever
symptoms.likely_causes: Infection (viral/bacterial), inflammation, heat exhaustion, immune response
symptoms.red_flags: Temp above 103°F/39.4°C, stiff neck, confusion, difficulty breathing, seizure
symptoms.self_care: Rest, fluids, light clothing, paracetamol/acetaminophen per label
symptoms.male_notes: May spike higher; higher metabolic rate. Recovery typically 5-7 days
symptoms.female_notes: Hormonal cycle affects baseline temp. Higher in luteal phase. May worsen PMS
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Fever lasts >3 days, or in infants under 3 months with any fever

symptoms.name: Frequent urination
symptoms.likely_causes: Excess fluid intake, UTI, diabetes, bladder irritation
symptoms.red_flags: Frequent urination with excessive thirst and fatigue (possible diabetes signs)
symptoms.self_care: Monitor fluid intake, avoid bladder irritants
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Sudden change in pattern or with other symptoms

symptoms.name: Headache
symptoms.likely_causes: Tension, dehydration, eye strain, migraine, sinus congestion
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden 'worst-ever' headache, headache with fever/stiff neck, or after head injury
symptoms.self_care: Rest in dark quiet room, hydration, OTC pain relief
symptoms.male_notes: Often tension-type. Less likely migraine (except cluster headaches more common)
symptoms.female_notes: Migraines 3x more common. Hormonal fluctuations trigger migraines. Estrogen withdrawal effect
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Frequent, worsening, or unlike usual headaches

symptoms.name: Hearing loss
symptoms.likely_causes: Wax buildup, infection, loud noise exposure, aging
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden hearing loss in one or both ears
symptoms.self_care: Avoid loud noise, do not use cotton swabs deep in ear
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Sudden or unexplained hearing loss

symptoms.name: Heartburn/acid reflux
symptoms.likely_causes: Spicy/fatty food, overeating, lying down after meals, GERD
symptoms.red_flags: Chest pain that could mimic heart issues, difficulty swallowing
symptoms.self_care: Smaller meals, avoid trigger foods, don't lie down right after eating
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Frequent (2+ times/week) or worsening

symptoms.name: High blood pressure symptoms
symptoms.likely_causes: Diet, stress, genetics, lack of activity
symptoms.red_flags: Severe headache with vision changes, chest pain, or confusion
symptoms.self_care: Reduce salt/stress, regular monitoring, activity
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Readings consistently above normal range

symptoms.name: Hives
symptoms.likely_causes: Allergic reaction, stress, infection, food/medication trigger
symptoms.red_flags: Hives with facial/throat swelling or breathing difficulty (anaphylaxis)
symptoms.self_care: Antihistamine per label, avoid trigger, cool compress
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Widespread, recurring, or with swelling of face/throat

symptoms.name: Insomnia
symptoms.likely_causes: Stress, anxiety, depression, caffeine, sleep apnea, poor sleep hygiene
symptoms.red_flags: Persistent severe insomnia, suicidal ideation, manic episodes
symptoms.self_care: Regular sleep schedule, avoid screens before bed, relaxation techniques, exercise
symptoms.male_notes: Often sleep apnea related (more common in men). Earlier onset age
symptoms.female_notes: Hormonal disruptions (perimenopause, menopause). Pregnancy-related. Postpartum insomnia
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts >2 weeks, significantly impacts daily functioning, or worsening

symptoms.name: Insomnia/sleep disturbance
symptoms.likely_causes: Stress, caffeine, screen time, irregular schedule
symptoms.red_flags: Chronic insomnia with mood changes or thoughts of self-harm
symptoms.self_care: Consistent sleep schedule, reduce screens/caffeine before bed
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persists beyond 3-4 weeks

symptoms.name: Irregular menstrual cycle
symptoms.likely_causes: Stress, hormonal changes, weight changes, underlying conditions
symptoms.red_flags: Severe pain, very heavy bleeding, or bleeding after menopause
symptoms.self_care: Track cycle, manage stress, balanced diet
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persistent irregularity or very heavy/painful periods

symptoms.name: Itching
symptoms.likely_causes: Dry skin, allergic reaction, insect bite, irritant
symptoms.red_flags: Itching with widespread hives and breathing difficulty
symptoms.self_care: Moisturize, avoid scratching, cool compress
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persistent, widespread, or affecting sleep

symptoms.name: Joint pain
symptoms.likely_causes: Arthritis, gout, injury, overuse, lupus, Lyme disease
symptoms.red_flags: Severe swelling, warmth, fever, sudden onset inability to move
symptoms.self_care: Rest, ice/heat therapy, compression, elevation, gentle stretching
symptoms.male_notes: Often sports/overuse related. Gout 4x more common in men
symptoms.female_notes: Autoimmune arthritis (RA) 3x more common. Hormonal changes affect joint inflammation
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts >2 weeks, accompanied by fever, or significantly limits mobility

symptoms.name: Loss of appetite
symptoms.likely_causes: Illness, stress, medication, digestive upset
symptoms.red_flags: Combined with severe abdominal pain or vomiting
symptoms.self_care: Small frequent meals, stay hydrated
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts more than a week or causes noticeable weight loss

symptoms.name: Loss of smell/taste
symptoms.likely_causes: Viral infection, sinus congestion, nasal polyps
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden loss with no other symptoms lasting weeks
symptoms.self_care: Saline rinse, allow infection to resolve
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persists beyond 2 weeks

symptoms.name: Memory loss/confusion
symptoms.likely_causes: Fatigue, dehydration, stress, medication side effects, aging
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden confusion, especially with fever, head injury, or slurred speech
symptoms.self_care: Rest, hydration, reduce distractions
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Sudden onset or progressively worsening confusion

symptoms.name: Migraine
symptoms.likely_causes: Triggers: stress, hormones, certain foods, sleep changes
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden severe migraine unlike prior ones, with confusion or vision loss
symptoms.self_care: Dark quiet rest, hydration, known trigger avoidance
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Migraines increasing in frequency or severity

symptoms.name: Muscle pain/soreness
symptoms.likely_causes: Overexertion, tension, minor strain, viral illness
symptoms.red_flags: Severe pain with swelling, weakness, or dark urine
symptoms.self_care: Rest, gentle stretching, hydration, warm compress
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persists beyond a week or is severe

symptoms.name: Muscle weakness
symptoms.likely_causes: Overuse, dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, nerve issues
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden one-sided weakness, facial drooping, slurred speech
symptoms.self_care: Rest, hydrate, balanced electrolytes
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Sudden onset or progressively worsening

symptoms.name: Nausea
symptoms.likely_causes: Food poisoning, gastroenteritis, migraines, pregnancy, medication side-effect
symptoms.red_flags: Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, signs of dehydration
symptoms.self_care: Small frequent meals, ginger, peppermint tea, avoid strong smells
symptoms.male_notes: Primarily GI or medication-related. Less common overall
symptoms.female_notes: Consider pregnancy, hormonal contraceptives, hormonal cycle. Morning sickness in pregnancy
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts >24 hours, accompanied by severe pain or fever

symptoms.name: Neck stiffness
symptoms.likely_causes: Poor posture, sleeping position, muscle strain
symptoms.red_flags: Stiff neck with high fever and headache (possible meningitis)
symptoms.self_care: Gentle stretching, warm compress, posture adjustment
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: With fever/headache, or lasts beyond a week

symptoms.name: Night sweats
symptoms.likely_causes: Infection, hormonal changes, medication side effect, anxiety
symptoms.red_flags: Drenching sweats with unexplained weight loss or fever
symptoms.self_care: Breathable bedding/clothing, track frequency
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Occurs regularly for more than a week

symptoms.name: Numbness/tingling in limbs
symptoms.likely_causes: Nerve compression, poor circulation, vitamin deficiency
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden numbness on one side of body, face drooping, slurred speech
symptoms.self_care: Change position, gentle stretching
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persistent, spreading, or affecting one side suddenly

symptoms.name: Painful urination
symptoms.likely_causes: Urinary tract infection, irritation, dehydration
symptoms.red_flags: Pain with fever, back pain, or blood in urine
symptoms.self_care: Increase water intake, avoid irritants (caffeine/alcohol)
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persists beyond a day or with fever

symptoms.name: Palpitations (irregular heartbeat)
symptoms.likely_causes: Caffeine, stress, dehydration, anxiety, heart rhythm issues
symptoms.red_flags: Palpitations with fainting, chest pain, or breathlessness
symptoms.self_care: Reduce caffeine/stimulants, relax, hydrate
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Frequent, prolonged, or with fainting/chest pain

symptoms.name: Rash
symptoms.likely_causes: Dermatitis, eczema, fungal infection, viral infection, drug reaction, allergies
symptoms.red_flags: Spreading rapidly, severe blistering, fever, difficulty breathing
symptoms.self_care: Moisturize, avoid irritants, cool compresses, oatmeal baths
symptoms.male_notes: Often fungal (jock itch) or contact dermatitis
symptoms.female_notes: Yeast infections more common. Hormonal triggers. Cosmetics/product reactions
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Spreads rapidly, severe itching, accompanied by fever or systemic symptoms

symptoms.name: Runny/stuffy nose
symptoms.likely_causes: Common cold, allergies, sinus infection
symptoms.red_flags: Thick discolored discharge with facial pain and fever
symptoms.self_care: Saline rinse, fluids, rest
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persists beyond 10 days or with facial pain

symptoms.name: Seizure
symptoms.likely_causes: Epilepsy, high fever (children), head injury, low blood sugar
symptoms.red_flags: Any first-time seizure, seizure lasting over 5 minutes, or repeated seizures
symptoms.self_care: Move away from hazards, do not restrain, time the episode
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Always requires medical evaluation

symptoms.name: Sensitivity to light
symptoms.likely_causes: Migraine, eye infection, eye strain
symptoms.red_flags: With severe eye pain or sudden vision change
symptoms.self_care: Dim lighting, sunglasses outdoors, rest eyes
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persistent or with headache/vision changes

symptoms.name: Shortness of breath
symptoms.likely_causes: Asthma, anxiety, chest infection, exertion, heart issues
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden severe breathlessness, blue lips, chest pain
symptoms.self_care: Sit upright, slow breathing, use prescribed inhaler if applicable
symptoms.male_notes: Usually indicates cardiac/pulmonary pathology. Take seriously
symptoms.female_notes: May be anxiety-related. Pregnancy-related dyspnea normal. Iron deficiency anemia contribution
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Any unexplained or worsening breathlessness

symptoms.name: Sore throat
symptoms.likely_causes: Strep throat, pharyngitis, viral infection, allergies, GERD
symptoms.red_flags: Severe difficulty swallowing, drooling, breathing difficulty
symptoms.self_care: Gargle with salt water, throat lozenges, warm tea with honey, rest voice
symptoms.male_notes: Similar presentation. Slightly higher risk of strep in children
symptoms.female_notes: May worsen with hormonal cycle. Consider candida with certain contraceptives
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts >1 week, severe pain, fever >101°F, difficulty swallowing

symptoms.name: Swelling in legs/ankles
symptoms.likely_causes: Prolonged standing/sitting, poor circulation, heart/kidney issues
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden one-leg swelling with pain/warmth (possible clot), or breathlessness
symptoms.self_care: Elevate legs, reduce salt intake, move regularly
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Sudden, one-sided, or with breathing difficulty

symptoms.name: Swollen joints
symptoms.likely_causes: Injury, arthritis, infection, overuse
symptoms.red_flags: Sudden severe swelling with fever or inability to move joint
symptoms.self_care: Rest, ice, elevation, compression
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Persistent swelling or with fever

symptoms.name: Unexplained weight loss
symptoms.likely_causes: Metabolic changes, chronic illness, stress, thyroid issues
symptoms.red_flags: Weight loss with persistent pain, blood in stool, or severe fatigue
symptoms.self_care: Track diet and weight; ensure adequate calorie intake
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Loss of more than 5% body weight in 6-12 months

symptoms.name: Vomiting
symptoms.likely_causes: Infection, food poisoning, motion sickness, migraine
symptoms.red_flags: Blood in vomit, signs of dehydration, severe abdominal pain
symptoms.self_care: Sip clear fluids, rest stomach, bland diet when able
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: Lasts more than 24 hours or with dehydration signs

symptoms.name: Wheezing
symptoms.likely_causes: Asthma, allergies, respiratory infection
symptoms.red_flags: Wheezing with severe breathing difficulty or blue lips
symptoms.self_care: Avoid triggers, use prescribed inhaler if applicable
symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: New or worsening wheeze, especially in children

injuries.name: Cut/Laceration
injuries.common_causes: Sharp object, fall, kitchen accident
injuries.first_aid: Clean wound, apply pressure to stop bleeding, cover with sterile bandage
injuries.red_flags: Deep wound, won't stop bleeding, exposed fat/muscle/bone
injuries.male_notes: Higher incidence in workplace/occupational injuries. Slower wound healing with age
injuries.female_notes: Similar treatment. Pregnancy affects healing speed. May be more visible scarring concern
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Deep, gaping, or won't stop bleeding after 10 min pressure

injuries.name: Abrasion (Scrape)
injuries.common_causes: Fall, friction against rough surface
injuries.first_aid: Clean with water, remove debris, apply antiseptic and bandage
injuries.red_flags: Signs of infection (pus, spreading redness, warmth)
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Signs of infection or large/dirty area

injuries.name: Puncture wound
injuries.common_causes: Nail, needle, animal bite, splinter
injuries.first_aid: Clean thoroughly, do not force out deep objects, cover
injuries.red_flags: Deep puncture, rusty object, near joint/eye, signs of infection
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Any deep puncture (tetanus risk) or from a dirty/rusty object

injuries.name: Bruise (Contusion)
injuries.common_causes: Blunt impact, fall, bump
injuries.first_aid: Ice pack (wrapped) for 15-20 min, rest, elevate if possible
injuries.red_flags: Rapid severe swelling, inability to move area, numbness
injuries.male_notes: Common in contact sports. Higher pain tolerance may delay seeking care
injuries.female_notes: May bruise more easily (genetic/blood clotting factors). Hormonal cycle affects bruising
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Severe pain, large swelling, or no improvement after 2 weeks

injuries.name: Sprain (Ankle)
injuries.common_causes: Twisting/rolling ankle, uneven surface
injuries.first_aid: RICE: Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation
injuries.red_flags: Unable to bear weight at all, visible deformity, severe swelling
injuries.male_notes: Higher incidence in sports. More likely inversion injuries
injuries.female_notes: Higher ankle sprain rate in women athletes. Hormonal factors (ligament laxity) in luteal phase
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Cannot bear weight, severe swelling, or no improvement in a few days

injuries.name: Sprain (Wrist)
injuries.common_causes: Fall onto outstretched hand, twisting
injuries.first_aid: RICE, avoid gripping/lifting with injured wrist
injuries.red_flags: Visible deformity, severe pain, numbness in fingers
injuries.male_notes: Often from fall on outstretched hand in sports
injuries.female_notes: Osteoporosis risk postmenopause increases severity. May be fall-related
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Deformity, severe swelling, or persistent pain

injuries.name: Strain (Muscle pull - Hamstring)
injuries.common_causes: Sudden sprinting, inadequate warm-up
injuries.first_aid: RICE, gentle stretching once pain subsides
injuries.red_flags: Sudden 'pop' sensation, inability to walk, large bruising
injuries.male_notes: Common sports injury. Higher muscle mass aids recovery
injuries.female_notes: Increased risk mid-cycle due to ligament laxity. Pregnancy affects all muscle strains
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Severe pain, inability to walk, or large bruise/swelling

injuries.name: Strain (Lower back)
injuries.common_causes: Heavy lifting, sudden twist, poor posture
injuries.first_aid: Rest briefly, ice/heat alternating, gentle movement as tolerated
injuries.red_flags: Numbness/weakness in legs, loss of bladder/bowel control
injuries.male_notes: Often occupational/lifting. Disc herniation more common
injuries.female_notes: Pregnancy causes significant strain. Postpartum recovery longer. Osteoporosis risk
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Radiating leg pain, numbness, or loss of bladder/bowel control

injuries.name: Fracture (Simple/Closed)
injuries.common_causes: Fall, direct impact, sports injury
injuries.first_aid: Immobilize area, apply cold pack, avoid moving the person unnecessarily
injuries.red_flags: Visible deformity, bone through skin, severe swelling, numbness
injuries.male_notes: Higher incidence before age 50. Usually trauma-related
injuries.female_notes: Osteoporosis risk increases significantly postmenopause. May occur with minimal trauma
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Suspected fracture always needs medical imaging/treatment

injuries.name: Fracture (Compound/Open)
injuries.common_causes: High-impact trauma, severe fall, accident
injuries.first_aid: Do not push bone back in; cover wound with clean cloth; keep still; call emergency services
injuries.red_flags: Bone visible through skin, heavy bleeding, shock symptoms
injuries.male_notes: Usually high-energy trauma (falls, accidents). Faster healing typical
injuries.female_notes: Similar trauma mechanism. Postmenopausal women at higher risk of complications
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always a medical emergency

injuries.name: Dislocation (Shoulder)
injuries.common_causes: Fall on outstretched arm, sports collision
injuries.first_aid: Immobilize in position found, do not attempt to relocate it yourself, ice pack
injuries.red_flags: Visible deformity, numbness/tingling in arm, no pulse in limb
injuries.male_notes: Higher incidence in contact sports. Faster typical recovery
injuries.female_notes: Genetic ligament laxity more common. Recurrent dislocations more likely. Slower recovery
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always needs medical relocation and evaluation

injuries.name: Dislocation (Finger)
injuries.common_causes: Jammed finger, ball sports, fall
injuries.first_aid: Immobilize, avoid trying to pop it back yourself, ice pack
injuries.red_flags: Numbness, severe deformity, no blood flow to fingertip
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Any suspected dislocation needs medical evaluation

injuries.name: Concussion / Mild Head Injury
injuries.common_causes: Fall, sports collision, blow to head
injuries.first_aid: Rest, monitor closely, cold pack on area (no swelling relief needed internally)
injuries.red_flags: Repeated vomiting, worsening headache, confusion, unequal pupils, loss of consciousness
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Any head injury with vomiting, confusion, or loss of consciousness — seek care immediately

injuries.name: Whiplash
injuries.common_causes: Car accident, sudden jolt to head/neck
injuries.first_aid: Gentle movement as tolerated, ice/heat, OTC pain relief
injuries.red_flags: Numbness/weakness in arms, severe neck pain, loss of bladder control
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Severe pain, numbness, or symptoms worsening after a few days

injuries.name: Burn (First-degree)
injuries.common_causes: Brief hot surface/liquid contact, sunburn
injuries.first_aid: Cool running water 10-20 min, do not apply ice, loose dressing
injuries.red_flags: Covers large area, or on face/hands/genitals
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Large area, or on sensitive areas (face, hands, groin)

injuries.name: Burn (Second-degree)
injuries.common_causes: Hot liquid/surface contact, flame, chemical
injuries.first_aid: Cool running water, do not pop blisters, cover loosely with sterile non-stick dressing
injuries.red_flags: Blistering over large area, signs of infection, on face/joints
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Blistering, large area, on face/hands/joints, or unclear how deep

injuries.name: Burn (Third-degree)
injuries.common_causes: Prolonged flame/chemical/electrical contact
injuries.first_aid: Call emergency services, cover loosely with clean cloth, do not remove stuck clothing
injuries.red_flags: Charred/white skin, numbness at site, signs of shock
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always a medical emergency

injuries.name: Frostbite
injuries.common_causes: Prolonged cold exposure, inadequate clothing
injuries.first_aid: Move to warmth, warm gradually with lukewarm (not hot) water, do not rub area
injuries.red_flags: Skin white/waxy and hard, numbness, blistering
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Any suspected frostbite needs medical evaluation

injuries.name: Chemical burn/exposure
injuries.common_causes: Contact with corrosive chemical, splash injury
injuries.first_aid: Rinse with large amounts of water for 15-20 min, remove contaminated clothing, call poison control/emergency
injuries.red_flags: Severe pain, eye involvement, large area affected
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always seek immediate medical attention

injuries.name: Eye injury (foreign object/scratch)
injuries.common_causes: Dust/debris, scratch from fingernail or object
injuries.first_aid: Do not rub; rinse gently with clean water; blink to encourage tearing
injuries.red_flags: Object embedded, vision changes, severe pain, chemical involved
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Object embedded, vision changes, or pain persists

injuries.name: Nosebleed (Epistaxis)
injuries.common_causes: Dry air, nose picking, minor trauma
injuries.first_aid: Sit forward, pinch soft part of nose for 10 minutes, breathe through mouth
injuries.red_flags: Doesn't stop after 20 min, heavy bleeding, after significant head trauma
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Doesn't stop after 20 minutes or is heavy/recurrent

injuries.name: Broken/Chipped tooth
injuries.common_causes: Fall, impact, biting hard object
injuries.first_aid: Rinse mouth with warm water, save any tooth fragment, cold compress for swelling
injuries.red_flags: Severe pain, tooth knocked out completely, visible nerve
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Any broken tooth should be seen by a dentist promptly

injuries.name: Insect bite/sting
injuries.common_causes: Mosquito, bee, wasp, ant
injuries.first_aid: Remove stinger if present, cold compress, antihistamine/anti-itch cream
injuries.red_flags: Facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing, widespread hives (anaphylaxis)
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Signs of allergic reaction or infection at site

injuries.name: Animal bite
injuries.common_causes: Dog/cat/wild animal bite or scratch
injuries.first_aid: Clean wound thoroughly with soap and water, apply pressure if bleeding, cover
injuries.red_flags: Deep wound, bite from unknown/wild animal, signs of infection
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always seek care for possible rabies risk and infection/tetanus

injuries.name: Electric shock
injuries.common_causes: Contact with live wire, faulty appliance
injuries.first_aid: Turn off power source before touching person; call emergency services; check breathing
injuries.red_flags: Loss of consciousness, burns, irregular heartbeat, difficulty breathing
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always a medical emergency, even if person seems fine

injuries.name: Blister
injuries.common_causes: Friction from shoes/tools, burns
injuries.first_aid: Leave intact if possible, cover with padded bandage, avoid popping
injuries.red_flags: Signs of infection (pus, spreading redness, warmth)
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Signs of infection or blister is very large/painful

injuries.name: Torn ligament (e.g., ACL)
injuries.common_causes: Sudden twist/pivot in sports, direct blow to knee
injuries.first_aid: RICE, avoid weight-bearing, immobilize if possible
injuries.red_flags: Pop sound at injury, immediate severe swelling, knee gives way
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always needs medical/orthopedic evaluation

injuries.name: Rotator cuff injury
injuries.common_causes: Repetitive overhead motion, fall, heavy lifting
injuries.first_aid: Rest, ice, avoid overhead activity, gentle range-of-motion as tolerated
injuries.red_flags: Sudden severe weakness or inability to lift arm at all
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Persistent weakness, pain at night, or limited range of motion

injuries.name: Tendonitis (overuse)
injuries.common_causes: Repetitive motion, overtraining, poor technique
injuries.first_aid: Rest the area, ice, gradual return to activity, gentle stretching
injuries.red_flags: Sudden inability to move joint, severe swelling
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Persistent pain despite rest, or worsening symptoms

injuries.name: Shin splints
injuries.common_causes: Running on hard surfaces, sudden increase in activity
injuries.first_aid: Rest, ice, supportive footwear, gradual return to activity
injuries.red_flags: Severe localized pain that could indicate stress fracture
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Pain persists despite rest or worsens with walking

injuries.name: Heat exhaustion/heat stroke
injuries.common_causes: Prolonged heat exposure, dehydration, overexertion in heat
injuries.first_aid: Move to cool area, remove excess clothing, cool with water/fanning, rehydrate
injuries.red_flags: Confusion, very high body temp, hot dry skin, loss of consciousness (heat stroke)
injuries.recovery_time: Hours to a day for exhaustion
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Heat stroke signs (confusion, no sweating, very high temp) is an emergency

injuries.name: Hypothermia
injuries.common_causes: Prolonged cold exposure, wet clothing, cold water immersion
injuries.first_aid: Move to warmth, remove wet clothing, warm gradually with blankets
injuries.red_flags: Confusion, slurred speech, slow breathing, loss of consciousness
injuries.recovery_time: Hours to days depending on severity
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Moderate-severe hypothermia is a medical emergency

injuries.name: Choking
injuries.common_causes: Food/object blocking airway
injuries.first_aid: Encourage coughing; if unable to breathe/speak, perform abdominal thrusts (Heimlich)
injuries.red_flags: Unable to speak/breathe/cough, turning blue, loss of consciousness
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always seek medical check after a choking episode

injuries.name: Drowning/Near-drowning
injuries.common_causes: Submersion in water, swimming accidents
injuries.first_aid: Remove from water, call emergency services, begin CPR if not breathing
injuries.red_flags: Any period of submersion with coughing, breathing difficulty, or altered consciousness
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always requires emergency medical evaluation, even if person seems recovered

injuries.name: Spinal injury (suspected)
injuries.common_causes: Fall from height, diving accident, high-impact collision
injuries.first_aid: Do not move the person; keep head/neck still; call emergency services immediately
injuries.red_flags: Numbness, paralysis, loss of bladder/bowel control, neck/back pain after trauma
injuries.recovery_time: Varies widely, long-term care often needed
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Always a medical emergency — do not move the person

injuries.name: Burns (Thermal)
injuries.common_causes: Contact with hot surfaces, steam, boiling water, flames
injuries.first_aid: Cool with running water for 15-20 mins, remove tight items, cover loosely
injuries.red_flags: Large area affected, blistering, loss of skin, difficulty breathing
injuries.recovery_time: 1-3 weeks for minor burns; severe burns require hospitalization
injuries.female_notes: Pregnancy affects pain management options. Healing may be delayed
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Burns >2-3 inches, deep, or on face/hands/genitals need medical attention

injuries.name: Head injury
injuries.common_causes: Falls, motor vehicle accidents, assaults, sports injuries
injuries.first_aid: Call 911 for loss of consciousness, monitor breathing, keep person still
injuries.red_flags: Loss of consciousness, vomiting, clear fluid from ears/nose, confusion
injuries.recovery_time: 2 weeks to months depending on severity; concussion needs medical evaluation
injuries.male_notes: Higher incidence. May underreport symptoms. Sports-related more common
injuries.female_notes: Pregnancy complicates imaging/treatment options. Postpartum mood changes post-concussion
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: ANY significant head trauma requires emergency evaluation

injuries.name: Ankle sprain (Grade II-III)
injuries.common_causes: Rolling ankle during sports/walking, stepping off curb, ligament tear
injuries.first_aid: Rest, ice (20 mins), compression wrapping, elevation, immobilization
injuries.red_flags: Severe swelling, inability to bear any weight, visible deformity
injuries.recovery_time: 2-6 weeks for Grade II; 6-12 weeks for Grade III; may need PT
injuries.male_notes: Higher incidence in male athletes. Faster return-to-play typical
injuries.female_notes: Hormonal cycle increases injury risk (lower ligament strength mid-cycle). Longer recovery
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Cannot bear weight, severe swelling, or no improvement in 48 hours

injuries.name: Laceration
injuries.common_causes: Cuts from sharp objects, falls, accidents
injuries.first_aid: Stop bleeding with pressure, wash with soap/water, apply antibiotic ointment
injuries.red_flags: Uncontrolled bleeding, gaping wound, deep penetration
injuries.recovery_time: 7-10 days for simple cuts; larger lacerations may need stitches
injuries.male_notes: Occupational/trauma related. Wound closure easier typically
injuries.female_notes: Pregnancy affects anesthesia options. Scarring may be cosmetic concern
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Deep lacerations, won't stop bleeding, or edges won't stay together

injuries.name: Muscle strain (Grade I)
injuries.common_causes: Overexertion, sudden movement, lack of warm-up
injuries.first_aid: Rest, ice (15-20 mins), compression, elevation, NSAIDs for pain
injuries.red_flags: Severe bruising, inability to move muscle, severe pain
injuries.female_notes: Hormonal effects on muscle recovery. Pregnancy increases strain risk significantly
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Severe pain, inability to function, or no improvement in 48 hours

injuries.name: Severe bleeding
injuries.common_causes: Deep wounds, arterial injury, significant trauma
injuries.first_aid: Call 911, apply direct pressure with clean cloth, elevate if possible
injuries.red_flags: Continuous heavy bleeding, blood spurting, dizziness, pale skin
injuries.male_notes: Consider trauma, alcohol use. Higher baseline hemoglobin
injuries.female_notes: Pregnancy complicates management. Menstrual bleeding disorders may predispose. Lower baseline Hgb
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: ALWAYS call 911 for severe bleeding; medical emergency

injuries.name: Heat exhaustion
injuries.common_causes: Prolonged heat exposure, dehydration, intense exercise in heat
injuries.first_aid: Move to cool area, remove excess clothing, apply cool water, drink fluids
injuries.red_flags: No sweating despite heat, confusion, loss of consciousness, body temp >104°F
injuries.recovery_time: 2-24 hours after cooling and hydration; may need hospital care
injuries.male_notes: Higher incidence in occupational settings. Sweat response more efficient
injuries.female_notes: Hormonal cycle affects thermoregulation. Higher core temp in luteal phase. Pregnant women at higher risk
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Symptoms don't improve in 30 minutes or signs of heat stroke appear

injuries.name: Concussion
injuries.common_causes: Head impact during sports, falls, accidents
injuries.first_aid: Stop activity, observe for confusion/dizziness, seek medical evaluation
injuries.red_flags: Loss of consciousness, severe headache, vomiting, slurred speech
injuries.recovery_time: 1-3 weeks with physical/cognitive rest; return-to-play protocol required
injuries.male_notes: Higher incidence in contact sports. May return-to-play faster per old protocols
injuries.female_notes: Longer recovery typical. Hormonal factors affect recovery. Postpartum mood effects
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: Any suspected concussion needs medical evaluation; required before return to activity

injuries.name: Allergic reaction (Severe)
injuries.common_causes: Peanuts, shellfish, medications, insect stings, latex
injuries.first_aid: Call 911, administer epinephrine auto-injector if available, lay person flat
injuries.red_flags: Difficulty breathing, throat swelling, hives, anaphylaxis signs
injuries.recovery_time: Requires emergency hospital care; variable recovery
injuries.male_notes: Similar presentation. Epinephrine dosing same weight-based
injuries.female_notes: Pregnancy affects medication choices. Certain triggers more common (cosmetics, latex in medical settings)
injuries.when_to_see_doctor: ALWAYS call 911 for severe allergic reactions; medical emergency
